# Novo-aktionærer: Vi vil se resultater, og det gør vi med Q3

**Feed**: borsen-podcast  
**Published**: 2026-11-04  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish investor podcast, sponsored by Saxo Bank, centres on Novo Nordisk's Q3 report. The underlying numbers beat expectations and guidance was raised, and the All Star portfolio managers stay committed long-term, with the Cagrisema launch in 2027 seen as the key catalyst. The panel also discusses a sector rotation from US tech into defensives that has helped Danish stocks, the Nasdaq 100 nearing a 10% correction on AI capex and cash-flow worries, and portfolio names: GN Store Nord, DSV, Coloplast (being sold by Peter Bækgaard), Genmab and Royal Unibrew. The overall view is cautiously constructive: Danske Bank expects a more cyclical run into year-end, while the stock pickers favour execution-driven Danish recovery cases.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 NOVO-B — Novo Nordisk | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Q3 beat, raised guidance, Wegovy pill outperforming; both managers hold into 2027; Lars recently bought; targets 300 then 400 during 2027.

#### Reasoning

Hosts (Johnny Madsen, Lars Hytting) see strong commercial execution and a growing total market. Wegovy pill sales beat and new markets are opening (UK, Germany, Australia). Expectations for Cagrisema are depressed, leaving room for upside surprise in 2027. The stock is now traded on results, and delivering is the path to rebuilding foreign investor trust.

#### Sell Triggers

- failed or weak Cagrisema launch in 2027
- Wegovy pill sales disappoint
- repeated large write-downs
- failure to rebuild foreign investor trust

> *"Lad os passere 300 og så se på 400 i løbet af 27."*

---

### 🟢 DSV — DSV | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Johnny: sold off in hysteria, still far too cheap after 20% rise; Schenker integration and synergies; expects big buyback 2027.

#### Reasoning

Johnny Madsen argues the integration timing slip is irrelevant for the long-term case. Showing full DB Schenker integration and road-division synergies should bring growth back, and he expects a massive buyback in 2027 (his own expectation, not announced). He is holding the stock.

#### Sell Triggers

- DB Schenker integration fails
- synergies not delivered
- customers not returning

> *"den er stadigvæk alt for billig i min optik"*

---

### 🟢 GN — GN Store Nord | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Lars' pick; pressed to bottom, enterprise growth from Evolve 3 could give relief; Hearing sale to Amplifon unlocks value.

#### Reasoning

Lars Hytting expects the Q3 report to show some enterprise growth from new headset launches and a strong, back-end-loaded year end. EU approval of the Hearing sale would bring in cash and a tradable ~16% stake in Amplifon, revealing value the market does not price.

#### Sell Triggers

- no enterprise growth in Q3
- EU objections to Hearing sale
- weak Q4 finish

> *"Og hvis vi får det, så er jeg ret sikker på, at vi vil se en stor lettelse i aktien."*

---

### 🟢 VWS — Vestas | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Lars puts 50% of hypothetical 100k in Vestas, expects Q3 upgrade, will hold it.

#### Reasoning

Lars Hytting's money-on-the-table pick. He expects an upgrade with Q3 and a good trading day, and plans to keep Vestas rather than flip it. Green stocks also rallied on the US midterms.

#### Sell Triggers

- no guidance upgrade at Q3
- adverse US policy for renewables

> *"Ja, men det skulle være en 50-50 med Mærsk og Vestas. Jeg forventer at se to opjusteringer."*

---

### 🟢 MAERSK-B — Maersk | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 60%

Lars expects Q3 upgrade and good day; will flip Maersk into broad Danish index.

#### Reasoning

Short-term trade: Lars Hytting expects an upgrade at Q3 and plans to sell Maersk on a good day and rotate into the broad Danish index.

#### Sell Triggers

- sell after positive Q3 reaction
- no upgrade at Q3

> *"Mærsk vil jeg så flippe på en god dag."*

---

### 🔴 COLO-B — Coloplast | **SELL** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Peter Bækgaard exits: weak Q4, LT organic growth target cut to 5-7%, ~25% EBIT margin, PE 34.5. Johnny disagrees (adj PE ~19, conservative guidance).

#### Reasoning

Portfolio manager Peter Bækgaard (quoted, not a panel host) is selling because of zero earnings growth and a high valuation, leaving only a 4-5% dividend-type return. Johnny Madsen disagrees: the new CEO set the bar low, the savings programme should lift margins above 25%, the 60-80% payout is attractive and upgrades are possible. View is mixed.

#### Sell Triggers

- thesis invalid if Coloplast beats and upgrades margin targets
- earnings growth resumes

> *"Jeg har den holdning, at med den værdiansættelse, som aktien har, så er der ingen grund til at eje den."*

---

### 🟡 GMAB — Genmab | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

After ~100% YTD on three positive trials, Lars trimmed near 3900; still positive but expects news-flow lull; commercial execution unproven.

#### Reasoning

Lars Hytting took profit while staying positive and may buy back later. Both hosts say the Q3 report won't be groundbreaking. The next catalysts are approvals and building its own sales organisation, and the stock may drift during a news lull.

#### Sell Triggers

- product approvals delayed
- weak commercial launch execution
- drift during news vacuum

> *"Jeg er stadig positiv på Genmap, men vi solgte den noget fra her, da den lå i 3900."*

---

### 🟠 RBREW — Royal Unibrew | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Ole Søberg: PE 13.8 vs fair 18, ~12%/yr plus dividends; Lars agrees it's not expensive but PepsiCo loss answer missing.

#### Reasoning

Cited view from Ole Søberg (Brock Milton Capital) is a reasonable return profile, though Carlsberg looks better. Lars Hytting shares the view that it is cheap, but the lost PepsiCo contract (~13% of revenue) has no solution yet. Johnny abstains.

#### Sell Triggers

- no replacement cola deal before 2028
- EPS consensus falls

> *"så aktien tilbyder en fornuftig afkastprofil"*

---

### 🟢 CARL-B — Carlsberg | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Ole Søberg's same PE-based calculation gives 17% per year plus dividend, better than Royal Unibrew.

#### Reasoning

Cited analyst (Ole Søberg) view: using the same expansion of the price-to-earnings multiple and consensus EPS growth, Carlsberg offers about 17% a year plus dividend, implicitly preferred over Royal Unibrew.

#### Sell Triggers

- consensus EPS growth disappoints
- valuation rerating does not occur

> *"Samme regnestykke på Carlsberg giver dog 17% om året, plus udbytte."*

---

### 🟠 MSFT — Microsoft | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Danske Bank's strategist favours beaten-down hyperscalers with positive cash flow; host names Microsoft as one.

#### Reasoning

Lars Skovgaard Andersen (Danske Bank) sees an opportunity in hyperscalers that have been hit hard but still have positive cash flow. He also notes stocks usually do well after midterms. The host gives Microsoft as an example. He does not usually comment on single stocks.

#### Sell Triggers

- cash flow turns negative
- AI capex keeps rising without returns

> *"Ja, en hyperscaler, der netop stadig har positiv cashflow ifølge det seneste regnskab, det er i hvert fald Microsoft."*

---
